intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: Most Popular Dog Breeds
intro.html:
Popularity in the dog world is not arbitrary. The breeds that consistently rank at the top of registration charts and ownership surveys earn their place through a combination of outstanding temperament, versatility, and the ability to fit naturally into modern human life. America's most popular breeds tend to be friendly, trainable, and adaptable — dogs that can live as comfortably in a city apartment as on a country farm, that get along with children and strangers, and that reward their owners' investment with loyalty and affection that few other animals can match.

This guide contains affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate, Wooffy earns from qualifying purchases.

The American Kennel Club has been tracking breed registrations in the United States for over a century, and similar organizations worldwide produce comparable data. These rankings shift gradually over time as cultural tastes change — the French Bulldog's meteoric rise to the top of popularity charts is one of the most dramatic recent examples, reflecting the global trend toward smaller, apartment-friendly companion breeds. At the same time, perennial favorites like the Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, and German Shepherd have maintained their top positions for decades, a testament to the enduring appeal of versatile, family-friendly working breeds.

In the AKC's 2025 ranking, announced March 18, 2026, the French Bulldog held the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row, and the Dachshund climbed to No. 5 for the first time since 2003. This guide profiles that top 10 in ranking order and explains what makes each one special, then lists the AKC's full top 100. Whether you're a first-time dog owner trying to find the right starting point, or a seasoned owner curious about breeds beyond your own experience, this list offers a tour through the dogs that have captured the hearts of millions of families worldwide — and explains exactly why.

care.label: Breeds
care.heading: What are the most popular dog breeds?
care.html:
Listed in AKC ranking order for 2025. For ranks 11 to 100, see the full top 100 below.

#1 French Bulldog

Small20–30 min10–12 yrs lifespan

The French Bulldog's rise to the most popular breed in America reflects its perfect fit for modern urban life: adaptable, affectionate, low-exercise, and endlessly charming with their bat ears and compact build. As a brachycephalic breed, they need protection from heat and are prone to respiratory issues—but their personality is irresistible.

Full guide →

#2 Labrador Retriever

Large60–90 min10–12 yrs lifespan

The Labrador Retriever held the top spot in America for over 30 consecutive years—a record that reflects the breed's extraordinary combination of intelligence, trainability, and genuinely gentle temperament. Equally at home as a service dog, hunting companion, or family pet, Labs are the standard against which other family breeds are measured.

Full guide →

#3 Golden Retriever

Large60–90 min10–12 yrs lifespan

The Golden Retriever's combination of intelligence, patience, and warmth has made it one of the most beloved breeds in the world. Consistently gentle with children and responsive to training, they excel as service dogs, therapy dogs, and family companions. Their enthusiasm for life is genuinely infectious.

Full guide →

#4 German Shepherd

Large60–90 min9–13 yrs lifespan

The German Shepherd's combination of intelligence, loyalty, and versatility has kept it among America's most popular breeds in AKC registrations. Used in virtually every working dog application—police, military, search and rescue, service work—they are also devoted, protective family dogs who excel with consistent training.

Full guide →

#5 Dachshund

Small20–30 min12–16 yrs lifespan

The Dachshund's iconic silhouette—long body, short legs, expressive eyes—has made it one of the most recognizable breeds in the world. Originally bred to hunt badgers underground, they are bold, curious, and surprisingly tenacious. Their adaptability to apartment life and loyal, entertaining personality explain their enduring popularity.

Full guide →

#6 Poodle

Large60–90 min10–18 yrs lifespan

The Poodle's reputation for intelligence is well-earned—they consistently rank among the most trainable breeds. Their hypoallergenic coat, athletic ability, and gentle temperament make them popular across all sizes. The Standard Poodle combines elegance and capability in a versatile, long-lived package.

Full guide →

#7 Beagle

Small–Medium45–60 min12–15 yrs lifespan

The Beagle's friendly, sturdy, and adaptable nature has made it one of America's most consistently popular breeds. Originally a scent hound for rabbit hunting, they are now primarily beloved family companions. Their compact size, cheerful temperament, and love of food make them highly trainable—though their nose can lead them astray.

Full guide →

#8 Rottweiler

Large60–80 min9–10 yrs lifespan

The Rottweiler's combination of power, intelligence, and loyalty has made it one of America's most popular large breeds. With proper training and socialization, they are calm, confident, and devoted family companions who are exceptionally loyal to those they love and natural protectors of their home.

Full guide →

#9 German Shorthaired Pointer

Large2+ hrs/day10–12 yrs lifespan

The German Shorthaired Pointer's surge in popularity reflects growing interest in active, versatile breeds. Equally capable as a gun dog and family companion, the GSP's intelligence, athleticism, and affectionate nature appeal to active families. They need substantial daily exercise but reward owners with extraordinary loyalty.

Full guide →

#10 Bulldog

Medium20–30 min (strictly weather-limited)8–10 yrs lifespan

The Bulldog's wrinkled face, shuffling gait, and gentle temperament have made it one of the most recognizable breeds in the world. Modern Bulldogs are calm, affectionate, and surprisingly good with children despite their tough appearance. As a brachycephalic breed, they need careful management in warm weather.

Full guide →

Also Worth Considering: Designer Crossbreeds

Two widely kept designer crossbreeds never appear in the AKC ranking, because the AKC doesn't register crossbreeds:

  • Goldendoodle — Golden Retriever x Poodle. Friendly, trainable, often low-shedding.
  • Labradoodle — Labrador Retriever x Poodle. The original designer doodle, energetic and adaptable.

See our full Best Doodle Breeds for Families guide for in-depth coverage of all six doodle hybrids.

special.label: Considerations
special.heading: How to Choose from the Most Popular Breeds
special.html:
Popularity is a useful starting point, but it should not be the primary reason you choose a breed. The most popular breeds earn their status through broadly appealing traits — friendliness, trainability, adaptability — but every breed still has specific needs and characteristics that may or may not suit your lifestyle. A French Bulldog is enormously popular but may not be right for someone who wants to run marathons with their dog. A German Shorthaired Pointer is a wonderful breed but demanding for a sedentary household. Use popularity as a signal that a breed is likely to be well-supported by trainers, vets, and clubs — then dig deeper to make sure the specific traits match your life.

Health should be a major factor in your research, particularly with the most popular breeds. Extreme popularity can drive irresponsible breeding practices and amplify genetic health problems. French Bulldogs and English Bulldogs suffer from significant brachycephalic (flat-faced) health issues that affect breathing, temperature regulation, and quality of life. Labrador Retrievers and Golden Retrievers are prone to hip dysplasia and certain cancers. German Shepherds can develop degenerative myelopathy and hip problems. Dachshunds are prone to spinal disc disease (IVDD). Choosing a puppy from a reputable breeder who health-tests their breeding stock is the single most important step in reducing the likelihood of preventable inherited conditions.

Consider the long-term commitment carefully. A Labrador Retriever purchased as a puppy today will likely be with you for 10–12 years. A Poodle may live 14–16 years. A Bulldog, unfortunately, may average only 8–10 years with health challenges along the way. The most popular breeds are popular in part because they form deep, lasting bonds with their families — which means the decision to bring one home deserves proportional care and thought. Research the breed thoroughly, meet multiple examples of the breed if possible, talk to owners, connect with breed clubs, and make sure your living situation, budget, activity level, and long-term plans are compatible with the dog you choose.

faq.q: What was the most popular dog breed in 2025?
faq.a: The French Bulldog. In the American Kennel Club's 2025 ranking, announced on March 18, 2026, the Frenchie was No. 1 for the fourth year in a row. It first took the top spot in 2022, ending the Labrador Retriever's 31-year run at No. 1. The rest of the 2025 top five were the Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, German Shepherd Dog and Dachshund. The ranking counts AKC registrations in the United States, so it describes American purebred registrations rather than dogs worldwide.

faq.q: How does the AKC decide which dog breeds are most popular?
faq.a: The AKC ranks breeds by the number of dogs of each breed registered with it during the year. The 2025 list ranked 202 recognized breeds, and the full top 100 is in the table above. Designer crossbreeds such as the Goldendoodle and Labradoodle are not AKC-recognized breeds, so they are not ranked. A drop of a few places does not always mean a breed is less common, since other breeds may simply have gained faster.

faq.q: Why has the French Bulldog become so popular so quickly?
faq.a: The French Bulldog's rise to the top of popularity charts reflects several converging trends: urbanization and the growth of apartment living (Frenchies are ideal city dogs), celebrity culture and social media (French Bulldogs photograph extremely well and have been popularized by high-profile owners), and a general trend toward smaller, lower-exercise companion breeds. Their relatively quiet nature (compared to other small breeds), manageable exercise needs, and affectionate personality make them practical for busy modern lifestyles. However, their popularity has unfortunately also driven irresponsible breeding, and many French Bulldogs suffer significant health problems — making careful breeder selection especially important.

faq.q: Is the most popular breed the best choice for a first-time dog owner?
faq.a: The most popular breeds tend to be popular partly because they are accessible to a wide range of owners, which does make several of them good choices for first-timers. The Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, and Beagle are all well-established as beginner-friendly breeds due to their trainability, stable temperaments, and forgiving nature. The Poodle is highly intelligent and can be excellent for first-time owners who commit to training. Breeds like the German Shepherd and Rottweiler, while popular, are more demanding and benefit from experienced handling. Choosing a breed whose needs and temperament genuinely match your lifestyle and experience level is more important than following popularity charts.

faq.q: Where should I get one of these popular breeds — breeder or rescue?
faq.a: Both are valid options, depending on your situation. A reputable breeder provides predictability — you can see health test results for the parents, meet the dam, and have confidence in what to expect from the puppy's temperament and size. Look for breeders who health-test, don't have puppies always available, and encourage you to visit. Rescue is another wonderful option — popular breeds are well-represented in rescues and shelters, and adult rescue dogs often have established temperaments, basic training, and immediate compatibility with your household. Breed-specific rescues for Labradors, Goldens, Bulldogs, and most popular breeds are widely available and do extraordinary work placing dogs in suitable homes.
